## Appearance

Anne is a tall, slender woman with a pale, flower-like complexion, luminous gray-green eyes, and thick, glossy auburn hair worn in soft curls or braids. As a child, she was scrawny and freckled with bright red braids, though her hair darkened as she grew older. She holds her head with a proud, graceful air and possesses an elusive, vivid charm that illuminates her face when she smiles.

## Personality

Possessing a vivid imagination and an intense passion for beauty, Anne is an imaginative dreamer who weaves romantic fancies into the world around her. She has a deep capacity for affection and a strong desire to be loved, placing great value on kindred spirits and true friendship. Though quick-tempered and impulsive when provoked, particularly regarding her looks, she is generous, warm-hearted, and forgiving. She approaches life with an irrepressible enthusiasm and optimism, striving earnestly to live up to her high ideals.

## History

Anne Shirley was mistakenly brought to Green Gables in Avonlea by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, who had intended to adopt a boy from an orphan asylum. Though initially reluctant, Marilla agreed to keep her. Anne quickly formed a passionate friendship with Diana Barry and developed a fierce rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe after he called her 'Carrots.' After two years of studying under Miss Stacy, she tied for first place on the entrance exams for Queen's Academy, where she subsequently won the Avery Scholarship. Following Matthew's sudden death, Anne gave up the scholarship to remain at Green Gables and support Marilla, taking the post of teacher at Avonlea School. During her two years as a teacher, she founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, helped Marilla raise the orphaned Keith twins, and reconciled her long-standing feud with Gilbert, becoming his close friend. After Mrs. Rachel Lynde moved into Green Gables to live with Marilla, Anne was able to attend Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Gilbert, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon. While at Redmond, she rented Patty's Place, rejected a proposal from Roy Gardner after realizing she did not love him, and graduated with High Honors in English. Admitting her love for Gilbert when he nearly died of typhoid fever, she accepted his proposal of marriage in Hester Gray's garden. They were married in the orchard at Green Gables and moved to a little white house on Four Winds Harbor, where Gilbert established his medical practice. There they suffered the loss of their firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, before welcoming a healthy son, James Matthew.

## Background by volume

- Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, to high school teachers Walter and Bertha Shirley, who both died of fever when she was three months old  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011), [v1 c5 P13](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0013)</sub>
- Brought up by hand by Mrs. Thomas until age eight, helping care for children  <sub>[v1 c5 P13](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0013), [v1 c5 P14](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0014)</sub>
- Lived with Mrs. Hammond for over two years caring for three sets of twins until Mr. Hammond died  <sub>[v1 c5 P14](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0014), [v1 c5 P15](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0015)</sub>
- Spent four months in the Hopeton Orphan Asylum before being brought to Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v1 c2 P19](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0019), [v1 c5 P15](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0015)</sub>
